Q: Why is my web.config setting for restricting user authorization not working correctly? A:

Fixing this error if windows authentication is added to project after it's been created

That's a mouthful. I was having this issue when I added Windows authentication to an existing project. There were a couple of key things that I needed to do before it works:

  1. In Solution Explorer, Click on the project and then push F4. This should open up the Project properties.

  2. In Project Properties and under the Development Server, make the following changes:

    • Anonymous Authentication: Disabled
    • Windows Authentication: Enabled

  3. Include the following in the Web.config under <system.web>:

    <authorization>
  <allow users="DOMAIN\user"/>
  <deny users="*"/>
</authorization>

  4. Still in the Web.config under <appSettings>:

    <add key="owin:AutomaticAppStartup" value="false"/>

This is what worked for me. If I'm doing something wrong, please let me know.

Hopefully this will help future individuals who are working with windows authentication after creating the project.

Q: Why does passing NULL to a variadic function trigger a static analyzer warning about undefined behavior? A:

For historic reasons, the C standard allows NULL to be either an integer constant expression with value 0 or such an expression cast to void *. So NULL could be defined as 0, which would have type int. It could even be 0L or 0ULL, which would have type long or unsigned long long, respectively, since these are also integer constant expressions with value 0.

Then the sentinel argument to your variadic function would have a type incompatible with the type of the strings you are passing. You could be passing int while the strings result in char *. When your function attempted to get the value of this sentinel argument using va_arg(…, char *), the behavior would not be defined.

Additionally, note that your string arguments have type char *, not const char *. Again, this is for historic reasons; const was not originally in C, so string literals had type char *, and this was not changed when const was introduced.

So, to make your sentinel argument exactly match the strings, you should pass (char *) NULL.

Note

You can use (const char *) NULL even though const char * is not compatible with char *. This is because the C standard makes some exceptions in what types may be used with va_arg. C 2024 7.16.2.1 says it will work if:

… both types [the actual type of the argument and the type passed to va_arg] are pointers to qualified or unqualified versions of compatible types;…

Q: MSSQL: left join multiple columns in three tables A:

Working without a net here but I believe you want something like this:

select 
    L.LeaseID AS 'LID', 
    I.Name AS 'Type', 
    L.StartDate AS 'Start', 
    L.EndDate AS 'End', 
    CONCAT(T1.FirstName, ' ', T1.LastName) AS 'Tenant1', 
    CONCAT(T2.FirstName, ' ', T2.LastName) AS 'Tenant2', 
    CONCAT(T3.FirstName, ' ', T3.LastName) AS 'Tenant3', 
    CONCAT(T4.FirstName, ' ', T4.LastName) AS 'Tenant4'
from Leases L
left join Intervals I ON L.Interval = I.Value
left join Tenants T1 ON L.Tenant1 = T1.TenantID
left join Tenants T2 ON L.Tenant2 = T2.TenantID
left join Tenants T3 ON L.Tenant3 = T3.TenantID
left join Tenants T4 ON L.Tenant4 = T4.TenantID

Q: How to launch a KDE konsole with multiple tabs running various progs? A:

This must be a one-liner or a bug report must be submitted. Every other common terminal has this option. I did some research and the "almost one-liner solution" is this:

  1. Create a file configuring your tabulators like so and name it, let's say "tabs":
   title: %n;; command: /usr/bin/htop
   title: %n;; command: /usr/bin/ncmpcpp

(The full documentation is at https://docs.kde.org/stable_kf6/en/konsole/konsole/command-line-options.html. The called command binaries are examples. The %n will name the tab exactly like the command)

  1. Execute it like so:

    konsole --tabs-from-file path_to_tabs_file/tabs

Result: A new konsole window with 3 tabs, running defined binaries and one empty prompt. I couldn't get a bash script to run. But I did just a few minutes of testing.

Q: How to detect editing a cell and mark a non-editable date of edit in another cell? A:

A Worksheet Change: Keep Initial Time Stamp

  • Determine a max range (adjust TARGET_RANGE_ADDRESS). Select it and unlock it's cells. Format it as Text.
  • Format the same rows in column A with the desired date format (e.g. mm/dd/yyyy hh:mm:ss).
  • Protect the sheet with a password (SHEET_PW) and copy the code to the required sheet module (right-clicking the sheet tab and selecting View Code opens the correct code window).

Sheet Module, e.g., Sheet1 (Not ThisWorkbook or Module1)

Option Explicit

Private Sub Worksheet_Change(ByVal Target As Range)
    
    Const TARGET_RANGE_ADDRESS As String = "B2:C21"
    Const DATE_COLUMN As String = "A"
    Const SHEET_PW As String = "123"
    
    Dim ws As Worksheet: Set ws = Target.Worksheet
    
    Dim trg As Range: Set trg = ws.Range(TARGET_RANGE_ADDRESS)
    Set trg = Intersect(trg, Target)
    If trg Is Nothing Then Exit Sub ' no cell of the target range changed
    
    Dim dcell As Range, durg As Range
    
    For Each dcell In Intersect(trg.EntireRow, ws.Columns(DATE_COLUMN)).Cells
        If Len(CStr(dcell.Value)) = 0 Then ' not populated; add to range union
            If durg Is Nothing Then
                Set durg = dcell
            Else
                Set durg = Union(durg, dcell)
            End If
        'Else ' already populated; do nothing
        End If
    Next dcell
    
    If durg Is Nothing Then Exit Sub ' all cells populated
    
    ws.Unprotect SHEET_PW
        Application.EnableEvents = False
            durg.Value = Now
        Application.EnableEvents = True
    ws.Protect SHEET_PW
    
End Sub
